source.title: Every Component is a Lookup: Token Attribution and Composition from a Single Decomposition
source.authors: Po-Kai Chen; Niki van Stein; A. Plaat

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different, observational graph-based method to check whether selected GPT-2 small IOI circuit connections appear in the claimed branches, and compares their credit coverage on IOI prompts and matched ABC controls.
record.gate_note: The IOI rerooting rankings and IOI-versus-ABC coverage comparison bear on the circuit and its task specificity. The paper's Pythia knockout results concern perplexity, not IOI; its greater-than results concern another circuit, not reuse of the IOI circuit. The token-attribution method comparisons and dispatch ablation do not test the claimed 26-head circuit criteria.
record.test_reason: A different, observational method (rerooted attribution graph, no patching) checks whether the IOI compositions Wang et al. named in GPT-2 small appear in their claimed K/Q/V branches, with matched ABC controls. This bears on V1 and on V4 (whether a different method recovers the same circuit). The study does not vary circuit-evaluation ablations or metrics, so V5 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that their observational graph recovers the IOI compositions established by path patching, branch by branch, including the Q- versus K-side distinction for S-Inhibition into Name Movers. Claimed components lose credit coverage on matched ABC controls, while layer-0 components behave like prompt-independent bias. Contribution is therefore not causal effect, and the method complements rather than replaces intervention.
record.recipe_differences: The original establishes IOI connections by path patching; this study reroots an observational attribution graph on a single forward pass and ranks upstream components by branch-specific credit, without patching.
record.method_sensitivity: The IOI-versus-ABC comparison changes coverage for claimed components, especially at source layers 2–6, while layer-0 coverage barely changes. In other experiments, perturbation faithfulness is at chance with β=0 and stable for β≥0.2; dispatch choice changes BOS token credit. The latter sensitivity results are not tests of the IOI circuit.

fits_no_version.finding: Token attribution shows S2 credit for predicting S below S1 credit and below the ABC copying baseline (E=1.09 in GPT-2 small). The S1–S2 gap is positive in all five Pythia-deduped models and weaker at 2.8B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The S-inhibition suppression signature in token credit at S2 appears across model scales.

record.problems: The IOI composition check uses n=100 prompts and observational credit rankings rather than interventions. It tests selected connections, not all 26 heads or the faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria. The matched-control coverage results are reported qualitatively from a figure.
record.rows_left_out: No additional IOI circuit results meeting the row criteria were omitted. Greater-than circuit results, Pythia perplexity knockouts, and attribution-method comparisons concern other tasks or measures.

untested.parts: The full 26-head, 7-class circuit; per-head membership (ranks are for the best member of a role tier); negative and backup name movers; faithfulness, completeness and minimality.
No ablation of name movers or test of backup heads.

No head-class circuit in other models or checkpoints. The Pythia results are perplexity knockouts and S2 token-credit gaps, not circuits. The greater-than results check Hanna et al.'s own circuit, not reuse of IOI components.
No comparison with ACDC, EAP or other ablation types or metrics. Only three compositions are checked.
No variation of ablation, metric or prompt distribution for the circuit's faithfulness or completeness.
No name-order, template or multi-name variants.

missing.what: Composition rankings with layer-0 heads included: Dup column moves to ranks 1–2 with near-100% coverage also on ABC; other median ranks rise by about 10.
Per-head coverage and credit share IOI vs ABC, e.g. S-Inh 8.6 credit share −59%, Ind 5.5 −92%, Dup 3.0 −95%, while layer-0 heads show no coverage change.
Full composition matrices across all modes and branches (e.g. S-Inh→NM in K mode 10/48%; Prev→S-Inh in V mode 10/21%).

record.verdict_notes: V5 labels removed: the IOI-vs-ABC comparison probes the attribution method's bias, not how faithful or complete the circuit looks under different evaluations. V4 added because the study's central IOI result is a different method recovering the claimed compositions. Ranks score the best-placed member of each role tier, so they do not confirm individual heads. n=100, no uncertainty reported, preprint.

versions.untested_parts: Tests selected claimed connections and task-specific credit patterns in GPT-2 small, not the complete 26-head, 7-class circuit or its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria as a whole.
No main-name-mover ablation or self-repair test.
No test that the same IOI head classes and roles recur in other models, sizes, or checkpoints, or that IOI components are reused for other tasks.
Does not compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or circuit-evaluation metrics for recovery of the IOI circuit.
Tests IOI versus matched ABC prompts for credit coverage, but does not systematically vary ablation type or evaluation metric.
No systematic test across name orders, sentence templates, or prompts with more names.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 small, IOI prompts (n=100), upstream pool of layer-≥1 heads
relationships.reason: Claimed roles rank 1–3 in their claimed branches with at least 95% found (r1, r3, r4, r5). S-Inh is weak on the K side as the circuit implies (r2). Claimed components lose 30–70 coverage points on ABC, unclaimed at most 19 (r6, r7).
relationships.display_finding: Proposed roles ranked 1–3 in their predicted branches with at least 95% recovered, while S-inhibition was weak on the key side; ABC corruption reduced coverage by 30–70 points for proposed components versus at most 19 for others.

source_check.reason: r1–r5 recover the selected compositions with the expected branch distinction; r6–r7 show greater task dependence for claimed components. This supports the tested connections.

relationships.reason: A non-patching method recovers the three claimed compositions branch by branch (r1–r5), and their credit is task-tied (r6, r7).
relationships.display_finding: The observational method recovered all three claimed compositions branch by branch, with attribution credit tied to the task.

relationships.reason: Layer-0 heads, including the claimed Dup heads, keep near-100% coverage on ABC, so the method cannot show them as task-specific (r8). Per the text (Table 7), including them raises other median ranks by about 10.
relationships.display_finding: Layer-0 heads, including the proposed duplicate-token heads, retained near-100% coverage on ABC, while including them raised other median ranks by about 10.

source_check.notes: Figure 3 uses paired controls restricted to prompts where A is not the top prediction; Table 8 instead pools branches over all 100 pairs. Recovery concerns selected compositions, not a test of whole-circuit faithfulness, completeness or minimality; the authors explicitly distinguish contribution from causal necessity.
